candidates.filename: Steamer ATHLON on Navy Yard Route at Colman Dock in Seattle, ca 1912 (TRANSPORT 858).jpg
candidates.caption:
PH Coll 794.9
Built by J.H. Johnston in Portland and sold March 27, 1901 to H.B. Kennedy of the Puget Sound Navigation Company. Contract price was $4,935. Length 112.4' Beam 19.7' Depth 7' Gross tonnage 157 Net tonnage 104. ATHLON operated on the Port Orchard - Seattle and Bremerton Navy Yard - Seattle route until 1914.1914: ATHLON operated by the Liberty Bay Transportation Co., an independent service competing on the Poulsbo - Seattle run.August 1, 1921: Puget Sound steamer ATHLON, operated by the Poulsbo Transportation Co. and in charge of Capt. Roy McMasters, struck Ludlow Rocks at the entrance to Port Ludlow in heavy fog. Ship total loss, 9 passengers and crew safely reached shore.1923: Kitsap County Transportation Co. bought machinery from wrecked ATHLON. (Source: Newell, Gordon, ed. "The H.W. McCurdy Marine History of the Pacific Northwest." Seattle: The Superior Company, 1966)
Subjects (LCSH): Athlon (Ship); Ships--Washington (State)--Seattle; Piers & wharves--Washington (State)--Seattle

"on Navy Yard Route" means on the run between Downtown Seattle and the Navy Yard at Bremerton on the Kitsap Peninsula.  This is still a Washington State Ferries route from the current Colman Dock over a century later.
candidates.sourceFamily: commons:Steamer ATHLON on Navy Yard Route at Colman Dock in Seattle, ca 1912 (TRANSPORT 858).jpg

candidates.filename: Steamer DEFIANCE at Colman Dock in Seattle, ca 1912 (TRANSPORT 875).jpg
candidates.caption:
Operated as part of the famed "Mosquito Fleet" of the Puget SoundPH Coll 794.31
The DEFIANCE was a 93 foot propeller steamer built by Matthew McDowell at Tacoma in 1900, replacing the DAUNTLESS on the Seattle-Tacoma-West Pass route. The name was changed to KINGSTON around 1913 and the ship was sold to the Whidby Island Transportation Co., serving Silverdale, Bainbridge Island, and other locations on the Kitsap Peninsula. The ship was converted to diesel power in 1933 for use as a fish hauler, but struck rocks at Whitestone Narrows on May 20 of that year. The KINGSTON, originally DEFIANCE, was a complete loss.  (Source: Newell, Gordon, ed. "The H.W. McCurdy Marine History of the Pacific Northwest." Seattle: The Superior Company, 1966)
Subjects (LCSH): Defiance (Ship); Ships--Washington (State)--Seattle; Piers & wharves--Washington (State)--Seattle

The other ship shown here is unidentified.
candidates.sourceFamily: commons:Steamer DEFIANCE at Colman Dock in Seattle, ca 1912 (TRANSPORT 875).jpg
